title: messaging: NotificationTemplateStore's locale ladder (named tag, primary subtag, en) never reads the stack's declared i18n.fallbackLocale
body:
domain:server#5 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5oc56xChD6Wrc4cGSt

Filing gate: ① the #28880 dev's out-of-scope finding (os-dev-report 6568876497), filed by `domain:server` seat 5. Graded by this seat: p3. The sibling ladder already folds the primary subtag, so only a declared fallback outside the recipient's language is missed. Graded under 「定级你可以自己决定」 (Leehom, 2026-11-01).

Reach: in-app, SMS and push notifications rendered from `sys_notification_template` for a recipient whose locale has no row, on a stack whose `i18n.fallbackLocale` names a locale other than `en`.
Reader who acts: a `domain:server` seat (`packages/services/service-messaging`).

## What happens

`NotificationTemplateStore` loads `(topic, channel, locale)` and walks a fixed candidate list: the named tag, then its primary subtag (`zh-CN` → `zh`), then `DEFAULT_LOCALE` (`en`). See the comment at `notification-template.object.ts` ~line 130. It never reads the stack's declared fallback (`i18n.fallbackLocale`, else `defaultLocale`, through the i18n service's `getFallbackLocale`). After PR #28917 (#28880), the email ladder does read it, so the two template families disagree for the same recipient and stack.

## Wanted

- Measure: does the store see the i18n service, and does any shipped stack declare a non-`en` fallback?
- If so, the declared fallback joins the ladder before `en`, folded by `resolveBundleLocale` if the store can read its locale list. ⛔ No third copy of the BCP-47 ladder.
- Tests red first, with an ablation. Update the comment at ~line 130 to the new two-resolver reading.

Blocked-by: #28880 (PR #28917 lands the email side this aligns with).

Dedupe: searched `NotificationTemplateStore fallbackLocale`; none. **New.**

Links back: #28880, PR #28917, #28896.
